transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, Doc. Well, I guess what finally got me in here is that... over these past few months, my mind just keeps jumping all over the place. 

I drive a truck for a living, and lately, every little thing pulls my attention away. It’s like my brain zeroes in on every chirp on the CB radio, every fuel price sign I pass by, or just some new idea that pops into my head. Because of it, I keep missing details that I normally never miss. I'm messing up things like a client’s delivery note, or I'll completely forget who I promised to call back. It's starting to get in the way of my work, so I figured I better come in and talk to somebody about it.
Before these past few months, did you have similar problems with attention or forgetfulness?

No, not really. It hasn't always been like this. It's just been going on for about... I'd say seven months now. That's right around the time my daughter moved back home. I've just been trying to keep everything steady around the house since then, and that's when I really started noticing the distraction and forgetfulness kicking in.
Since your daughter moved back home, have you been feeling excessively worried or on edge?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... it's an adjustment having her back, sure, but I'm not sitting around stressing or feeling on edge about it. I don't really feel worried. It's just... well, it's really just that my mind won't stay put on one thing, like I was saying. But no, no real worry or anything like that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
No, not really. I mean, I'm not feeling down or sad or anything like that. I'm just... easily distracted, like I said. But my mood itself is fine. I'm not depressed.
Do you feel that your trouble concentrating is mainly because of difficulties related to your daughter moving back home?

No, I don't think so. I mean, her moving back was an adjustment, sure, but we get along fine. We don't argue or anything. It's just that the timing lines up with when I started noticing my mind wandering off. I don't think she's the cause of it, it's just... that's when it started happening.
How has your sleep been since these attention problems began?

It's been pretty short, actually. Most nights I sleep... maybe three or four hours, tops. Then I'm up way before daylight. The funny thing is, I don't even feel tired. I just wake up feeling ready to roll instead of worn out, so I usually just get up and start my day.
During this period of sleeping only three or four hours, have you felt unusually energized or “up” compared with your usual self?

Yeah, I guess I have. For months now, actually. I've been feeling either way too fired up—just feeling like everything is going to work out great no matter what—or... well, or I'm snapping at people over really small stuff around the house and out in the yard. Which really isn't my usual way of doing things. But yeah, definitely feeling a lot more up than normal.
Have you ever been hospitalized because of a period when you felt unusually energized or irritable?

No, I haven't. I've never been in the hospital for anything like that. I mean, I've been feeling pretty fired up lately, like I said, but it hasn't ever gotten bad enough to put me in the hospital or anything.
How much have these energized or irritable periods interfered with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Well, it's definitely getting in the way somewhat. At work... I've been having trouble keeping things straight. Like, I've had to ask dispatch and my clients to repeat details that I really should have remembered. And I missed a couple of important sales follow-ups just because my mind was going in a hundred different directions at once. Then at home, it's... it's tough. My wife and daughter, they've been kind of walking on eggshells around me. I can tell I'm just adding stress to the house when I really should be helping out.
Have these changes ever made you unable to work or take care of your usual responsibilities?

No, not completely unable. I mean, I still show up for my routes every day. I haven't had to call out or take time off. Like I was saying, it makes things a bit harder, and I might mess up a detail here and there, but I'm still getting the job done. And at home, I'm still taking care of my stuff... just maybe with a bit more of an attitude. So, no, it hasn't actually stopped me from working or anything like that.
Have you ever had a sustained period when you felt significantly depressed or lost interest in most things?

No, I can't say that I have. I mean, sure, everybody gets a little down sometimes or has a bad day on the route, but... no, I've never had a long stretch where I felt really depressed or just lost interest in doing things. I usually just keep plugging away.
Has there been a distinct period of at least four consecutive days when you felt unusually energized or irritable most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, definitely longer than four days. Honestly, it's been going on for months now. I'll have these stretches where I'm just... really fired up, you know? Like I'm totally convinced everything is going to work out perfectly, no matter what. But then, just as often, I'm snapping at people over the smallest things. Like, out in the yard or at home, I'll just lose my temper over nothing. It's really not my usual way of doing things.
During these fired-up periods, have you been noticeably more active or taking on more projects than you usually do?

Yeah, I guess I have been. I just... I can't really seem to sit still lately. If I'm not moving, I get real antsy. So I just keep finding extra jobs for myself. Like, I've been rewriting all my route plans, trying to make them more efficient. And even after my shift, I'm sticking around, checking up on the new drivers, making sure they're doing things right. Then I get home and I'm fixing things around the house that haven't bothered me in years. It's just... I always have to be doing something right now.
During these fired-up periods, have you felt unusually confident in your abilities or believed you could accomplish things that would normally seem unrealistic?

Yeah, I actually have. Like, recently I got it in my head that I could rebuild the whole driver training program by myself. I just figured I could make it run way better than the bosses ever could. Which... you know, that's really not my lane at all. I just drive the routes. But at the time, I was completely sure I could pull it off without a problem.
During these fired-up periods, have you heard or seen things that other people could not?
No, nothing like that. I mean, I get pretty worked up, but I'm not... I haven't been seeing things or hearing voices or anything. It's just my own thoughts going a mile a minute, really.
